See, you most wicked one: now you did not come to Christ, but Christ of his own accord came down to you, he who was able to die without death, who begot all things and established all things, and did not create you alone, envious one. For venerable Scripture says: "God did not make death." So if you wish to know the stuff of your origin: you were conceived of the serpent as father and born of guilt as mother, but now, as pardon reigns, you are being consumed.

Meanwhile the Lord's spirit had already departed from his body for a time, and Christ's cold limbs hung on the wood of the cross; and still fury, not laying down its arms, put a spear into an enemy's hand, and with a wicked thrust violated the Lord's side with a wound, opening a deep, penetrating gash, through which blood and water flowed out together. O how this matter accords with catholic teaching! How these sacraments agree with faith in the Trinity! For body, blood and water are three gifts of our life. All of us who give ourselves to Christ as our leader are reborn in the fount of waters, and receiving his body and blood we eat and drink, that we may be worthy to be a temple of the Holy Spirit. For the apostle Paul also speaks thus: "Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?" Let us pray that the Lord may bid us keep that temple spotless, so that so great an indweller may make us, narrow and slight as we are, fit and spacious for himself.

After that holy place, then, had received the treasure of the precious body laid there—a place that shone with renown while the Lord lay in it and triumphed with greater renown when he rose—the generation devoted to deceit, devising its customary wickedness in its impious heart, kept spreading word that Christ would be carried off in the silence of night by his disciples stealing him away, so that it might be noised abroad that he had risen after the third day, just as he had foretold. Alarmed, then, by this suspicion of theft, the Jews asked that a very large guard be set with great care, and that the doors and entrance of the tomb be hemmed in by a most reliable watch. If, executioners, even after the bitter torments of the cross, after the blows and wounds of iron, after the mortal burial of the body, you have not yet fulfilled your bloody office, nor sated your unjust hatred after the death of the innocent, and do not rather acknowledge that the Lord of singular power, who so often led souls out of the underworld, will call back his own: then carry out the schemes that suit you, for the worse; nurse in your minds treacheries armed with the nourishment of perfidy; seal the bars of the tomb, post military watches, close the monument with a stone; and, having equipped everything with malicious arrangements, as you are doing, say: Who will be able to guard God, to whom all things lie open and nothing is barred? He reigns in heaven, commands the seas, and rules even the underworld. Why, then, disorderly mob, do you waste your effort in vigils and toil? Why do you strive to test a faith which you will not accept even when it is proved to you?

Meanwhile, after that sad sabbath, the festal day had begun to shine, the day most dear to the Lord who reigns, which takes its name from his majesty and is called by this honour the Lord's Day, since it attained such dignity that it was the first worthy to behold the origin of the world at its birth and the power of Christ at his rising. For thus the book of Genesis, the clear declarer of things, says that on the seventh day, the sabbath, God rested from his works. It is plainly evident, then, that this day is the head of the world, from which, as the first, the seventh, the sabbath, is counted in fixed order; and the glory of the eternal King, making it illustrious also with the trophy of his resurrection, decreed that it should hold, with reverence, the primacy granted it over all days.

At the bright rising of this light, the virgin mother, with the other women faithfully gathered with her, who had come to the Lord's tomb bearing together their gift of spices, furrowed their faces with tears and shook their breasts with groans. And soon they saw the place of burial lying open, empty now of the body, but overflowing, full of wonderful power. For an angel had come down from heaven and sat, wondrous to see, on the stone rolled away from the doors of the tomb, fiery in countenance, white in garments, so that, shining with a twofold diversity, he displayed terror and joy alike: terror, as he threatened the guards with his fiery face; joy, as he cheered those seeking Christ with the brightness of his snow-white robe. So the women, strengthened by the angel's revelation, rejoiced that the Lord had come back to life after death.

But the soldiers, terrified by such a sight, could scarcely keep hold of life, placed as they were in a perilous plight; and at once they deserted their post and rushed headlong back to the city, reporting the miracles and announcing plain facts free of charge. Then, after they had sold their faith for a price, they turned to a base falsehood, and soon they invented the tale that Christ's disciples had lain in wait in the quiet of the night and snatched him away. Tell us, wicked and shameless guard; speak, criminal legion: what do you mean to assert? In your eagerness to get money you do not see the pit of your own fall and danger, nor do you know how much punishment you deserve, since you prefer to seem negligent rather than truthful. For it is agreed that you were wakeful, careful and sharp-eyed, that you never let your eyes close in sleep unless the colleague next to you duly took his turn to relieve you in your labour, and that you so fortified the place with watches that it plainly could not be approached by any trickery. Was Christ, as you dare to concoct with lying voice, snatched from the tomb by the hands of his followers at night while you were at rest—he whose linen cloths lie there, whose wrappings lie there, by whose cast-off grave clothes angelic power sits? Or did the one who stole the blessed body first strip and bare it, thinking it could be taken away more quickly uncovered than carried off bound as it lay, when delay is the enemy of rapacious theft, and it could have been carried off more safely and secretly together with the Lord's wrappings? Iniquity has lied to itself. Yet this matter holds the excellent grace of a figurative sense. For it is clear that Christ has been taken away from the Jews spiritually, Christ whom we carry with the whole devotion of mind and heart. Lament, then, Judea, for your priests; lament for your ministers and your people. Forsaken for such great crimes, you will no longer rejoice in the trumpet, be strengthened by anointing, or enjoy sacrifices. In hope of whose power will the trumpet be blown for you, when you see your king slain? What anointed one will any longer be given you, when you have lost the rule of the Anointed himself? What victim will be struck, when the shepherd himself has been slaughtered as the victim? Let the synagogue depart, darkened now by its own colour: Christ has joined to himself the Church, beautiful with snow-white grace.

She shows forth the honour and glory of Mary, who, though she is always seen with manifest clarity to be the mother of the Lord, is nonetheless always seen to be a virgin. To her the Lord showed himself at once after the triumph of his resurrection, so that his loving and kind mother might make known the testimony of so great a miracle, and so that she who had been the door of his birth when he came into the world should also be the messenger of his departure from hell.

Soon afterward he joined certain people at a meal, as if he were a passing traveller, and in the breaking of bread he revealed himself to their senses and eyes; because, since he himself is the true bread, he makes himself known to those eyes which inner faith unlocks and uncovers, leading them by the brightness of grace to recognize the Lord.

Often, too, at various times and moments he showed himself plainly to the disciples: now appearing unexpectedly as they were eating, now taking food of broiled fish and honeycomb, to teach more plainly that the meal was a bodily matter; and by eating it he proved to those who watched that he now bore the same limbs he had borne a little before.

Again, when the apostles, fearing to suffer the violent savagery of the people who had so often denied the Lord, stayed in the house with the doors shut, he suddenly stood there though the doors were bolted, and gave peace to all with a word of greeting, so that, granting joy in return to the afflicted, he might confirm what he had foretold through the prophetic voice: that the Lord will not forsake a contrite and humbled heart. And at once he opened his pierced hands and bared the wound inflicted on his side, lest they believe him a phantom if they did not see the marks of his wounds.

But since Thomas, an apostle no less to be revered, who was called by the name Didymus, was not present there, and did not believe his companions when they reported these things, behold, afterward, when he was sitting with the brothers, the Lord, who had never departed from them in spirit, again presented himself to them, though the doors had not moved; and, appearing in the midst before all, he did not disdain to humour the trembling disciple. Showing once more his hands and side, he allowed himself to be put to the test by the touching of his wounds, and was the more surely recognized as being the Christ because he received the doubter's mind and cherished it with calm gentleness. For whoever practises crafty deceits under the blind semblance of fraud, and contrives empty mists and figures to deceive unwary minds, does not want to be examined, does not want his doings known, so that he may lurk under the veil of a deceptive cloud; and, mocking wretched eyes with fabricated phantoms, he hates those who look closely, even his friends, once he begins to be found out. But the Lord Christ, true in all things and most gentle even to one who doubts and hesitates to believe, is not angry with the waverer, but with mild readiness allows him even to plunge his fingers into the wounds, knowing that the example of this proof concerns not only Thomas, who was already blessed, but the faith of many in times to come.

A few days later the Lord again showed himself on the seashore to Peter, who was fishing with his companions. Seeing that, weary after toiling awake all night, they had caught nothing, he bade them let down the nets into the sea on the right side; and at once the water of the deep was enclosed, and the bulging, creaking folds drew out an immense gathering of fish with the catch, which they joyfully threw down before the Lord's feet. A miracle of this kind, then, ought not to be taken as an ordinary event, but weighed with a figurative understanding. For let us believe that the nets are the commandments of God, exceedingly bright and clear, in which all who follow the right hand, to be rescued from the waves of the world, are enclosed, bowed down at the feet of Christ.

For the fish laid on the coals, and the bread found by them in the same place, are also seen to carry the meaning of the catholic faith. The fish seems to stand for water, in which we are certainly washed and born again; the bread signifies Christ the Saviour, whose body we eat for our salvation; the fire bears the image of the Holy Spirit, by whom we are devoutly consecrated to the faith. For he appeared shining in this very form when, as the book of their Acts bears witness, he flooded the blessed apostles with his radiant divinity. Then he invites them to take the meal with the gentle bidding of his customary words, and they, gathering at once with one mind at the Lord's table, receive the food of holy blessing and recognize Christ with the full truth of faith.

When they had risen from the modest meal, suitably filled, the Lord gently asks him [?] whether he loves him. And as Peter at once assented, the Lord, wishing like a good shepherd to increase his flocks, entrusts his sheep and lambs to him as to a most faithful and proven worker. He repeats this a third time and goes over it again, so that the threefold denial of his recent fault might be cleansed by an equal number of declarations of love. That he gave Peter in particular the honour of feeding the flock, although it is evident that he loves all alike, does not detract from the others but seems to be in keeping with reason. For this most gentle animal, in the simplicity of its nature, is likened to the righteous, whom the King of all, when he comes in his majesty, will address in a different way as they stand at his right hand, as he himself taught: “Come, you who are blessed by my Father, take possession of the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world,” and so on. Fittingly, then, he entrusts the righteous who are to enter the kingdom to the one to whom he had promised to give the keys of that same kingdom.

Then, instructing them with blessed counsels and strengthening them by handing on his teaching of peace, he commands them to spread the precepts of the holy faith through all the earth and to bestow on all nations the one Trinity of holy baptism, speaking and decreeing thus: “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth. Go now and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, teaching them to keep all that I have commanded you,” and so on.

When he had commanded that all the things of his divinity be fulfilled, he soon led them out with him to Bethany, and there, before the very eyes of those blessed men who were found worthy to receive the vision of so great a triumph, he was carried up through the regions of the sky, ascended the citadel of his starry dominion, and sits at the right hand of the Father's majesty. He rules and governs all things by his own will, he who, possessing for ever all things high and deep, came down after heaven into the underworld, and after the underworld returned to heaven. He chose to pass to the stars while they were present for this reason (so far as he deigns to open it to my small understanding): to show them the road by which they were to follow. For before his passion, when they said to him, “Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way?”, he answered plainly and said, “I am the way and the truth and the life.” The way, because through him one comes to the Father's grace; the truth, because he gives believers what he promises; the life, because those whom he adopts are not subject to death. So the disciples, full of joy, watching the Lord high above the clouds, having conquered the world, tread with his own feet the shining tracts of the stars, humbly venerate and worship him. And in their most welcome return they turn over in their hearts the regions of the airy path that had served his steps, which they had seen with their eyes, and carry the news back, to urge all nations to believe. For they are shown to be faithful and the greatest witnesses of divine power, who saw the countless deeds of the Lord Jesus Christ and wrote down a few of those noble acts. For if all the miracles of our Saviour could have been bound into sacred pages, perhaps not even the world itself, as John the evangelist testifies, could hold all the volumes of books that would be written.
